considered_and_not_triggered.reason_considered: DPDP erasure-cascade + per-subject crypto-shredding + India-region bucket provisioning is a high-consequence privacy/legal surface (OAQ-10 flags crypto-shredding-as-erasure as a legally unsettled question).
considered_and_not_triggered.reason_not_triggered: Applying the three literal criteria: it does not touch Zone 7 itself (it touches Zone 8), it does not modify the ZoneRepository PORT interface (it modifies the Zone 8 adapter's internal read/write behavior behind the existing port, exactly as ar1_assignments.json AR1-002 distinguished 'implements a zone adapter' from 'modifies the port interface'), and its per-tenant in-region bucket provisioning is data-RESIDENCY, not cross-TENANT isolation (a tenant's own data staying inside its own region is a different property from one tenant being unable to see another tenant's data, which is what AC-008-3/threat I-5 in DASH-STORY-018 actually tests). Literal application of the stated criteria therefore does not fire here, exactly as ar0_routing_index.json's own operating rule requires (apply stated criteria literally, do not invent new ones). This is recorded as a routing gap (AR1-S2-G1) with a non-blocking advisory-review recommendation instead of a P1 gate, since asserting a P1 that is not supported by the stated criteria would be the same kind of unstated adoption the Sprint 1 file explicitly avoided for DASH-STORY-003's DPDP obligation (AR1-G3).
